prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Desktop Idle Posture", "Select how your desktop pet rests on your screen while you work.", "Choose Posture"]
1: ["Sign In to Keep Your Pet Safe", "Log in with your existing account to restore existing pets or back up your new companion.", "Continue with Existing Account", "Signing in ensures your pets sync across reinstalls."]
2: ["Your Companion Is Awake!", "Your pet is now active on your desktop screen."]
3: ["Explore Companion Styles", "Compare pre-made friends with custom photo creation before deciding.", "Continue to Selection"]
4: ["Preparing desktop graphics assets and companion physics...", "Rendering desktop companion engine"]
5: ["Your pet lives on your desktop! Right-click the tray icon to interact, hide, or summon your companion anytime."]
6: []
7: ["Already have a pet? Sign in with your original account to restore your companion without starting over."]
8: ["Fastest Setup: 1 Minute"]
9: ["We'll notify you when your desktop pet is ready to play."]

verdicts.problem: Implies collecting contact details to send notifications
